children.html: Sumbawa Diving: Dive Sites in West Sumbawa

children.classes: elementor-element elementor-element-622e5ad3 elementor-widget elementor-widget-text-editor
children.html: Beneath the waves, every glance is a discovery. Dive uncrowded reefs, mantas and walls off the West Sumbawa coast with Mocean Beach Resort.

content.classes: elementor-element elementor-element-5812831 e-flex e-con-boxed rt-default-class e-con e-parent

children.classes: elementor-element elementor-element-6579ecf elementor-widget__width-initial elementor-widget-mobile__width-inherit elementor-widget elementor-widget-text-editor
children.html:
Sumbawa diving is still one of Indonesia’s best-kept secrets. Off the west coast you get uncrowded reefs, manta rays that chain-feed at Ju-Ju’s Jackpot, walls and drift dives on the outer reefs, and a house reef you can walk into from the beach, all without the boat traffic of Bali or the Gilis.

Mocean Beach Resort runs its dive centre right on Pantai Moro in West Sumbawa. We keep groups to no more than four divers per guide, plan each day around the tide, and take you to the sites that suit your level and the conditions.

children.html:
Why Dive Here

Is Sumbawa Good for Diving?

children.classes: elementor-element elementor-element-6579ecf elementor-widget__width-initial elementor-widget-mobile__width-inherit elementor-widget elementor-widget-text-editor
children.html:
Yes, especially if you prefer quiet reefs to busy dive sites. West Sumbawa sits in the Coral Triangle, one of the richest marine areas in the world. Very few dive operators work this coast, so on most days ours is the only boat on the site.

The diving here suits a wide range of divers:

  • New divers get calm, sheltered bays and a shallow house reef for check-out dives and first open water dives.
  • Experienced divers get outer reefs with stronger currents, walls, drop-offs and drift dives.
  • Manta lovers get Ju-Ju’s Jackpot, where manta rays chain-feed in plankton-rich water.

Dives last 45 to 65 minutes. Proof of dive insurance is required before you arrive.

The Best Dive Sites in West Sumbawa

children.html:
The house reef starts just offshore from Pantai Moro, so you can walk in from the beach. It is our site for relaxed shore dives, check-out dives after a break from diving, and training dives for PADI courses.

At night the house reef changes completely. Crabs, octopus and sleeping parrotfish come out under the torchlight, which makes it one of the easiest night dives in Sumbawa. A shore dive or night dive costs IDR 1,540,000.

children.html:
Ju-Ju’s Jackpot is our manta site, named after Julie, our first instructor. Manta rays chain-feed here in plankton-rich water, sweeping past in a line with their mouths wide open. The most famous regular is Polong, a black “ninja” manta with a white mark on his belly.

Even without mantas, the reef is busy. Anthias flicker over the coral, reef sharks and black snappers patrol the edges, and the current brings in the plankton that keeps the whole site alive. Mantas are wild animals, so sightings depend on conditions and are never guaranteed. Our page on manta rays in Sumbawa has photos, video and the story of Polong, plus the best way to book a manta dive.

children.html: Kenawa is a small island off the West Sumbawa coast, and the reefs around it make a longer boat trip worth the time. It is our special-trip site, booked when the weather and sea conditions line up. The two-tank trip to Kenawa costs IDR 2,750,000. Ask us about conditions when you book.

children.html:
The rest of our Sumbawa diving splits into two kinds of site. Sheltered bays give calm, easy dives for newer divers, with gentle slopes and plenty of reef fish. The outer reefs bring stronger currents, walls and drop-offs for experienced divers.

On drift days the current carries you along wide reefs and coral walls. These are some of the most exciting dives on this coast, and our guides choose the timing carefully around the tide.

children.html:
PADI Courses

Learn to Dive in Sumbawa

children.classes: elementor-element elementor-element-6579ecf elementor-widget__width-initial elementor-widget-mobile__width-inherit elementor-widget elementor-widget-text-editor
children.html:
You do not need to be certified to dive with us. Discover Scuba Diving lets you try diving with a PADI instructor from IDR 1,980,000, starting in the calm water of the house reef.

If you want to get certified, our PADI dive centre teaches courses from Open Water through to Rescue Diver, with no more than two students per instructor. Our page on PADI dive courses in Sumbawa explains each course and what it costs, so you can pick the right starting point.

children.html:
Built for Divers

Our Dive Centre and Boat

children.classes: elementor-element elementor-element-6579ecf elementor-widget__width-initial elementor-widget-mobile__width-inherit elementor-widget elementor-widget-text-editor
children.html:
The Mocean dive centre is built for divers. There is a spacious wet area, private lockers and an air-conditioned camera room to keep your equipment and footage safe. We dive from a custom-built dive boat with a sun deck, and every dive is led by a local guide who knows the sites, the currents and the mantas.

After diving you are a few steps from your room, the pool and Mutiara, our beachfront restaurant.

Beyond West Sumbawa

More Diving in Sumbawa: Whale Sharks in Saleh Bay

children.classes: elementor-element elementor-element-6579ecf elementor-widget__width-initial elementor-widget-mobile__width-inherit elementor-widget elementor-widget-text-editor
children.html: Saleh Bay, on the north coast of central Sumbawa, is known for whale sharks that feed near the fishing platforms (bagan). It is several hours by road east of West Sumbawa, so most visitors go on an overnight trip. If you want to add it to your Sumbawa diving holiday, our guide to things to do in Sumbawa covers it along with the island’s other highlights.

children.html:
Is Sumbawa good for diving?

Yes. West Sumbawa has uncrowded reefs in the Coral Triangle, manta rays at Ju-Ju’s Jackpot, walls and drift dives on the outer reefs, and a house reef you can walk into from the beach. Most days ours is the only boat on the site.

When is the best time to dive in Sumbawa?

April to October has the clearest water and the most stable weather. Our dive season runs from 1 April to 31 October.

Can I see manta rays in Sumbawa?

Yes. Manta rays chain-feed at Ju-Ju’s Jackpot, one of our West Sumbawa dive sites. They are wild animals, so sightings depend on conditions and are never guaranteed.

How much does diving in Sumbawa cost?

A two-tank boat dive with Mocean costs IDR 2,200,000, or IDR 2,750,000 to Kenawa. Full gear rental is IDR 330,000 a day.

Do I need to be certified to dive?

No. Discover Scuba Diving lets you try diving with a PADI instructor from IDR 1,980,000. Certified divers can join daily fun dives.

How many divers are in each group?

No more than four divers per guide, so every dive is small and personal.

What is the visibility like in Sumbawa?

On average 10 to 15 metres, and best during the dry season from April to October.
